skill.name: segment-automation
skill.description: Automate Segment event, identity, group, page, alias, batch, and source workflows through the Rube MCP toolkit.
skill.summary: Discover current Segment tool schemas and execute validated customer data workflows through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 55 external-command alerts and three reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and ordinary validation or privacy guidance. The Rube MCP endpoint is a real network dependency, and the workflows can expose customer data or perform irreversible identity and source changes.

remediation.issue: Customer data passes through the Rube MCP service.
remediation.suggestion: Document Rube and Composio data handling, and require users to verify the endpoint, tenant, permissions, and approved fields before connecting.
Require explicit confirmation that displays previousId and userId immediately before every alias operation.
Preview source changes and require explicit confirmation before execution. Include rollback guidance when the current Segment schema supports it.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Segment connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `segment`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- `timestamp`: ISO 8601 timestamp (optional; defaults to server time)
- `context`: Object with contextual metadata (IP, user agent, etc.)
- At least one of `userId` or `anonymousId` is required
- `event` name is required and should follow consistent naming conventions
- `traits`: Object with user properties (email, name, plan, etc.)
- At least one of `userId` or `anonymousId` is required
- To remove a trait, set it to `null`
1. `SEGMENT_BATCH` - Send multiple Segment calls in one request [Required]
- `batch`: Array of message objects, each with:
- Each message in the batch must have a valid `type` field
- `traits`: Object with group properties (name, industry, size, plan)
- `groupId` is required; it identifies the company or organization
- `properties`: Object with page-specific properties (url, title, referrer)
- At least one of `userId` or `anonymousId` is required
- `name` and `category` are optional but recommended for proper analytics
- `previousId` is the anonymous/old ID, `userId` is the new/identified ID
- Always include `userId` or `anonymousId` on every call
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Avoid sending PII in traits unless destinations are configured for it
- Each message in the batch must have a valid `type` field
- Avoid sending sensitive PII unless destinations are configured for it

content.value_statement: Manual Segment calls are error-prone, and schemas can change. This skill discovers current tools and guides authenticated event, identity, group, page, and batch operations.
actual_capabilities: Finds current Segment tool schemas through RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS before building calls.
Guides Segment connection setup and checks for an ACTIVE status.
Sends track, identify, group, page, alias, and batch calls.
Applies required identifiers, timestamps, traits, properties, and event naming guidance.
Explains asynchronous acceptance, batch errors, and rate-limit considerations.
Lists and updates source settings using available Segment tools.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an authenticated Segment connection.
Depends on current Rube and Segment schemas, permissions, limits, and destination behavior.
Successful API acceptance does not confirm delivery to every destination.
Alias operations are one-way, and source updates can disrupt data collection.

use_cases.title: Track Product Engagement
use_cases.description: Send consistent track and page calls with validated identifiers, names, properties, context, and timestamps.

use_cases.title: Prepare Batch Imports
use_cases.description: Validate mixed Segment messages and send them efficiently while preserving per-message error handling.

use_cases.title: Maintain Customer Identities
use_cases.description: Identify users, assign organization groups, and review identity aliases with controlled traits.

prompt_templates.title: Track One Event
prompt_templates.prompt: Search current Segment tools and confirm the active connection. Track {event_name} for {user_id} with these approved properties: {properties}.

prompt_templates.title: Identify and Group a User
prompt_templates.prompt: Find current schemas. Identify {user_id} with approved traits {traits}, then associate the user with {group_id}. Show proposed calls before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Segment batch for {messages}. Validate message types, identifiers, timestamps, and required fields. Summarize all validation failures before sending.

prompt_templates.title: Review Sensitive Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect source {source_id} and propose {configuration_change}. Assess aliasing {previous_id} to {user_id}. Require my explicit confirmation before either write.

output_examples.input: Track an Order Completed event for user 4821 with approved order details.
output: Schema validation: user identifier, event name, and required properties are present.
Result: Segment accepted the event for asynchronous processing.

output_examples.input: Prepare a batch containing page, identify, and track messages.
output: Three messages reviewed against the current schema.
One identify message needs a user or anonymous identifier.
The valid messages are ready after the missing identifier is supplied.

output_examples.input: Link anonymous visitor anon-18 to customer 4821.
output_examples.output: Proposed alias: anon-18 becomes customer 4821. This one-way identity change requires explicit confirmation before execution.

best_practices: Search current tool schemas before every workflow and validate connection status.
Preview identifiers, event names, traits, aliases, and source changes before writes.
Minimize personal data and confirm destination policies before sending traits or context.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse stale schemas or guess parameters.
Do not send aliases or source updates without explicit confirmation.
Do not treat an accepted response as proof of downstream delivery.

faq.question: What connection does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Rube MCP and an authenticated Segment connection with permissions for the requested operations.

faq.question: Does it discover current Segment parameters?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs the agent to call RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS before workflows because schemas and limits can change.

faq.question: Can it send multiple message types together?
faq.answer: Yes. SEGMENT_BATCH supports track, identify, group, page, and alias messages when each message satisfies its requirements.

faq.question: Does acceptance confirm destination delivery?
faq.answer: No. A successful response means Segment accepted the request for asynchronous processing, not that every destination received it.

faq.question: How does it handle personal data?
faq.answer: The skill warns against sensitive data. Users must approve fields and verify Rube, Segment, and destination privacy controls.

faq.question: Can an identity alias be reversed?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents aliasing as a one-way operation, so identifiers must be reviewed before execution.
